Our experience at this clinic was profoundly negative, especially regarding how they handle animal stress.

During a consultation, they categorically refused to allow us to stay with our cat during the examination. They told us the animal had to be taken to another room, without its owners, and even stated that "in Portugal, this is how it is everywhere." This simply does not correspond to our experience: we have been treated at other clinics in Portugal where owners stay with the animal during the examination.

For me, this is one of the cruelest and unnecessarily stressful approaches that can be adopted with an already sick and frightened animal.

An animal doesn't understand that it's in a clinic or that those people want to do it good. It feels bad, is removed from its environment, transported to an unfamiliar place, surrounded by strange smells and people, and then separated precisely from the only people it knows and trusts. The cat is taken by strangers to another room, where it may be handled and subjected to potentially uncomfortable or painful procedures, without even being able to see, hear, or feel the presence of its owner to seek reassurance.

I cannot understand why another stress factor is deliberately added when there is no concrete medical need to separate the animal from its owner.

This is particularly difficult to accept because the “2022 AAFP/ISFM Cat Friendly Veterinary Interaction Guidelines,” specific international recommendations for the welfare and handling of cats in a veterinary setting, advocate precisely the reduction of fear, anxiety, and so-called “stressor stacking.” These same recommendations indicate that, except when there are insurmountable obstacles, outpatient procedures should also be performed in the consultation room to avoid separating the cat from its caregiver. They also recommend that the examination be done, whenever possible, in the place and position chosen by the cat—including in the owner's lap.

These guidelines also explain that a negative veterinary experience can create lasting emotional associations: pain and fear during a consultation can cause the cat to associate the veterinary clinic itself with fear and threat in future visits.

Naturally, I fully understand that there are procedures in which the owner's presence is not possible—surgery, anesthesia, certain diagnostic techniques, sterility or safety issues. That's not what I'm talking about. I'm talking about an apparently automatic policy of separating the animal from its owner even during a normal evaluation, without first trying a less stressful approach adapted to that animal.

The Statute of the Portuguese Order of Veterinarians itself establishes that veterinary activity must be carried out with adequate scientific and technical knowledge and with respect for animal life, and the promotion of animal welfare is part of the Order's responsibilities.

For me, animal welfare is not just about correctly diagnosing and treating a disease. It's also about not causing avoidable fear and suffering during that treatment.

A veterinary clinic should be a place where we try to reduce the fear of a vulnerable animal, not a place where the first decision is to remove its only source of safety at that moment.

After this experience, we will not return.
They are very professional and very friendly.

If you're looking for a clinic to care for your animals, run away from this one. My cat has always been calm, but when seen by the veterinarian, he became aggressive, and she and her assistant, instead of calming him down or using proper techniques, lost their temper in a completely unprepared manner, causing my pet to injure his paw. The clinic is completely unprepared and staffed by inexperienced professionals. My three animals will never go near this place again.

Terrible service.

I needed an urgent appointment.
I've been waiting since 3 AM for them to open and they tell me to come back at 3 PM.

Inconsistency in the care provided to our pets.

Furthermore, they present themselves as partners of insurance companies and inflate the prices.

A quote of €234.25 for a tartar removal, with Fidelidade insurance it would be €160.96.
At another clinic, the same service, without any discount, costs €65.

Don't be fooled. It's outrageous to see this kind of practice.
